topic: Biosphere reserves of India — mixed tiers
description: MAB programme, India's 18 reserves, UNESCO-recognised, key states + ecosystems

questions.stem: The concept of Biosphere Reserves is associated with which UNESCO programme?
questions.explanation: MAB (Man and the Biosphere) Programme — UNESCO, launched 1971. Biosphere Reserves are 'science for sustainability' sites — combining biodiversity conservation with sustainable use. Three zones: (1) CORE — strictly protected, no human disturbance; (2) BUFFER — limited research, education, eco-tourism; (3) TRANSITION — communities live and work, sustainable practices. India has 18 designated biosphere reserves (national list); 12 of them are also part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR). India joined WNBR with Nilgiri (2000).

questions.stem: India's FIRST Biosphere Reserve, designated in 1986, is:

options.option_text: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka)

questions.explanation: Nilgiri — 1st BR, designated 1 Sep 1986. Spans Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka (parts of all three). Includes Bandipur, Mudumalai, Nagarhole, Mukurthi NPs and Wayanad WLS, Silent Valley NP. Ecologically rich — Western Ghats endemics (Lion-tailed macaque, Nilgiri tahr, Nilgiri langur). UNESCO WNBR 2000. Often confused with Nanda Devi (designated 1988, 2nd BR). Sequence of first 5 Indian BRs: Nilgiri (1986), Nanda Devi (1988), Nokrek (1988), Manas (1989), Sundarbans (1989).

questions.stem: The COLD DESERT Biosphere Reserve, located in Himachal Pradesh, includes which national park?
questions.explanation: Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve — designated 2009; covers Pin Valley NP, Chandratal + Sarchu wetlands, Kibber WLS in the Lahaul & Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh. Habitat of the elusive snow leopard (Pin Valley). Hemis NP — in Ladakh, separate (largest NP in India by area, ~4,400 km²; not in HP). Khangchendzonga — Sikkim BR (UNESCO 2018, also a World Heritage Site). India's 18 BRs by approximate region: Western Ghats (4 — Nilgiri, Agasthyamala, NBR core, Gulf of Mannar coastal); Eastern Himalaya (4 — Nanda Devi, Khangchendzonga, Nokrek, Dibru-Saikhowa); NE (2 — Manas, Dehang Dibang); Central India (3 — Achanakmar-Amarkantak, Pachmarhi, Panna); Coastal/Islands (2 — Great Nicobar, Sundarbans); Cold Desert (1 — HP); Salt-marsh (1 — Kachchh, Gujarat); Aravalli (1 — Pachpadra/Sariska area as proposed) — totals approximate.

questions.stem: The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, India's first MARINE biosphere reserve, lies along which coast?

options.option_text: Coast of Tamil Nadu (between India and Sri Lanka)

questions.explanation: Gulf of Mannar BR — declared 1989; India's FIRST marine BR. Stretches ~140 km along Tamil Nadu coast from Rameswaram in the north to Kanyakumari in the south. 21 small islands; ~3,600 km² of coral reefs, mangroves, seagrass beds, salt marshes. Habitat of dugong (sea cow — endangered), corals, sacred chank, dolphins. UNESCO WNBR 2001. The Kachchh BR (Gulf of Kutch — 2008) is in Gujarat. Bhitarkanika in Odisha is a notable mangrove + olive ridley site but a Ramsar site / NP, not a BR.

questions.stem: Which biosphere reserve, located in Madhya Pradesh, was added to the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2009 and contains the Bori sanctuary, Pachmarhi and Satpura NPs?
questions.explanation: Pachmarhi BR — Madhya Pradesh, designated 1999; UNESCO WNBR 2009. Includes Pachmarhi NP, Bori WLS, Satpura NP. Located on the Satpura range; rich in deciduous forests, gorges, waterfalls (Bee Falls, Apsara Vihar). 'Queen of Satpuras' — Pachmarhi hill station. Achanakmar-Amarkantak BR — straddles MP + Chhattisgarh, includes the source of Narmada. Panna BR — MP, around Panna Tiger Reserve. Kanha-Pench — separate tiger reserves (not a single BR).

questions.stem: The largest biosphere reserve in India by area is the:

options.option_text: Cold Desert BR (~7,770 km², Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh)

questions.explanation: Cold Desert BR — ~7,770 km², largest in India by area. Spans Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur districts of HP. Other large BRs: Gulf of Kachchh (~7,506 km²), Sundarbans (~9,630 km² — actually slightly larger than Cold Desert depending on the boundary delineation; both are sometimes quoted as #1). Smallest BR — Dibru-Saikhowa (~765 km², Assam). 18 BRs total; 12 of them in UNESCO WNBR. Most recent UNESCO addition — Panna (2020). Note: the area-ranking order shifts with revised boundary maps; the conventional answer for 'largest' is the Cold Desert / Gulf of Kachchh in older sources and Sundarbans in newer reckonings.

questions.stem: Which UNESCO-recognised Biosphere Reserve in the Northeast spans Sikkim and shares its territory with the world's third-highest mountain peak?
questions.explanation: Khangchendzonga BR — Sikkim. UNESCO WNBR 2018. Surrounds Mt Kanchenjunga (8,586 m, world's 3rd highest peak — India's highest peak; on India-Nepal border). The Khangchendzonga National Park within it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (Mixed natural + cultural, 2016) — recognising both biodiversity (snow leopard, red panda, blue sheep) and the mountain's sacred status to the Lepcha people. Manas BR — Assam, royal Bengal tiger + golden langur + pygmy hog + hispid hare, also a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985, originally listed as 'in danger' due to insurgency, removed from danger list in 2011). Nokrek — Meghalaya, citrus genetic diversity centre. Dibru-Saikhowa — Assam, river-island ecosystem.
